bounds: One legacy Shared room, up to three serialized requests, up to two background history reads, one complete ordered history pair, and one caller deadline per request.
limitations: The modeled failure is an authoritative history read that rejects before local publication. Success abstracts archive writes, snapshot storage and acknowledgement as one settled operation. Failure during those writes, ambiguous acknowledgement, concurrent eviction and tombstones are outside the bound.

The caller deadline returns a retryable warming result while its original background read remains owned. A later request may join that read or start another after a failed read settles. The fair proof gives no wall-clock deadline and does not guarantee a successful dependency outcome.

The Workerd suite runs the real Durable Object, SQLite storage and request path. The history repository response is controlled to exercise delay and failure. The model excludes personal rooms that intentionally start empty, canonical authorization, actual PostgreSQL and provider composition.

assumptions: No fairness. The deadline replies to the one waiting caller and leaves the existing history read in progress.
Weak fairness of either the caller deadline or an enabled reply continuation. A reply can indicate warming rather than success.
Weak fairness of the background dependency settling. A lookup can return the complete ordered history or fail.
No fairness. The caller timer, dependency response and continuation can all remain pending.
